introduction.text: Casino di Villa Boncompagni Ludovisi is a historic building in Rome’s Ludovisi district, notable for its Renaissance architecture, artistic treasures, and its role in the cultural life of the city.

history.description: Cardinal Francesco Maria Del Monte established a suburban retreat in the 16th century, creating the original villa that would become Casino Ludovisi.
From 1549 to 1627, Del Monte collected art and patronised figures such as Galileo and Caravaggio, and commissioned works for the villa.
In 1621, Del Monte sold the villa to Ludovico Ludovisi, who expanded the property into a 30‑hectare park.
In 1883, the Boncompagni‑Ludovisi heirs subdivided and sold the estate, leading to the development of Rome’s Ludovisi district.
The property was put up for sale in 2021 following the death of Prince Nicolò Boncompagni‑Ludovisi.
An auction was held in 2022 with a starting bid of €471 million.
In 2023, Princess Rita was evicted from the premises after a court ruling.

design.description: The casino’s architecture was designed by Domenichino, featuring classical proportions and a grand staircase.
The surrounding gardens were attributed to André Le Nôtre, reflecting French formal garden style.

art.description: Caravaggio’s ceiling painting Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto, the only ceiling work by the artist, adorns a small room in the casino.
Guercino’s fresco of Aurora in the main reception hall gives the casino its alternative name, Casino dell’Aurora.
The collection includes works by Pomarancio (Niccolò Circignani) and Michelangelo, as well as Roman and Greek artefacts.
